Therefore every start the entrypoint COPIES the runner into the writable run directory: rm -rf /home/runner/runtime/* then cp -a /opt/runner/. /home/runner/runtime/ (a plain copy; no hard links, because /opt/runner is in the image layer and the run directory in the container layer, and hard links would let the runner modify image files through copy-up semantics in ways that are not worth reasoning about). Then it copies the three files from the named volume codesign-runner-state (mounted at /home/runner/state, nothing else) into /home/runner/runtime. The volume never holds binaries, so a new image always runs its own RUNNER_VERSION. facts.F507: Provider, not engine, by construction. osslsigncode 2.10+ with -pkcs11module first tries the provider named by -provider and silently falls back to the libp11 engine when the provider does not load (source: osslsigncode.c sign key loading). Because the image carries no pkcs11 engine, that fallback cannot sign: a provider load failure fails the step loudly instead of signing through the engine. The sign command is: osslsigncode sign -provider pkcs11 -pkcs11module /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/opensc-pkcs11.so -key pkcs11:id=%01;type=private -pkcs11cert pkcs11:id=%01;type=cert -ac tools/codesign/SSL_COM_CODE_SIGNING_INTERMEDIATE_CA_ECC_R2.crt -readpass - -n "Lighthouse VERSION" -i https://letpeople.work/lighthouse -t http://timestamp.digicert.com -in FILE -out FILE.signed. The image sets ENV PKCS11_PROVIDER_MODULE to the opensc module because the latchset provider reads that variable, not the PKCS11_MODULE_PATH that osslsigncode exports. The provider is also configured with pkcs11-module-quirks = no-deinit (tools/codesign/openssl-pkcs11.cnf, installed as /etc/ssl/openssl-pkcs11.cnf): with osslsigncode 2.13 and pkcs11-provider 1.2.0, osslsigncode crashes (exit 139) when the provider shuts the PKCS#11 module down at process exit, even after a good signature; skipping that shutdown costs nothing because signing is a short-lived process and the sign step stops pcscd right after. The file includes the system OpenSSL config and declares the pkcs11 provider section with the quirk.

Lifecycle carrier: shell state in the one script process. The script exports PKCS11_PROVIDER_MODULE=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/opensc-pkcs11.so itself, so it does not depend on the image ENV. Order: (1) look for a USB device with idVendor 1050 under the sysfs root (default /sys/bus/usb/devices, overridable by CODESIGN_USB_SYSFS for the oracle); none: print plug in the YubiKey and re-run this job, exit 1, no pcscd, no PIN read. (3) wait at most CODESIGN_READER_WAIT seconds (default 10) for opensc-tool --list-readers to list a reader; timeout: the plug-in message plus a hint to run tools/codesign/check-host.sh, exit 1, PIN never read. (4) sign the server exe, the NSIS exe and the MSI, PIN on stdin from YUBI_PIN, never argv, never echoed, no set -x, no retry of a failed file. (5) the trap stops pcscd on every exit.
